_comment: Authored analysis: ownership, lifecycle, refcount and locking judgements that no composer can derive, keyed to the C entities they describe. The structural half of each record (field layout, signatures, footprints, casts) is composed from the CodeQL tables on demand and merged in at read time, so a re-extract rewrites nothing here. Written only by `crustify-oracle <target> query {types,symbols} --update`; read through crustify.manifests. Hand-edit at your own risk: `--update` validates a submission against the composed skeleton (unknown field, wrong kind, ptr-invariant violation) and this file does not.

types.name: ASN1_ITEM_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_ITEM instances and every pointer they publish are immutable function-local static descriptors generated by asn1t.h macros; no lifecycle routine owns or releases the descriptor storage.

ptr.note: Optional process-lifetime descriptor selected by itype; it aliases a static ASN1_PRIMITIVE_FUNCS, ASN1_EXTERN_FUNCS, or ASN1_AUX value and is never freed through ASN1_ITEM.
All public ASN1_ITEM definition macros store a process-lifetime string literal; consumers use it directly as a non-null C string.
Process-lifetime static const template storage: null for types without templates, a singleton for ASN1_ITEM_TEMPLATE, or an array of tcount elements for SEQUENCE/CHOICE.

types.name: ASN1_TEMPLATE_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_TEMPLATE values are generated as static const descriptors by the public asn1t.h macros. They own neither their item callback nor their field-name string.

ptr.note: ASN1_EX_TYPE and ASN1_EX_TEMPLATE_TYPE initialize this const char pointer with a stringized identifier, yielding a non-null immutable static NUL-terminated string.
ASN1 template macros initialize this slot with an ASN1_ITEM_ref function symbol. Templates are static const descriptors, so the callable is non-null, immutable, and process-lifetime borrowed.

types.name: ASN1_VALUE_st
types._comment_agent: OpenSSL deliberately never defines ASN1_VALUE_st; include/openssl/asn1.h documents it as an opaque type-erased pointer equivalent to void *. It has no layout or lifecycle of its own.

types.name: BIO_sock_info_u
types._comment_agent: BIO_sock_info_u is a caller-owned transient argument union. Its sole current variant borrows mutable BIO_ADDR storage for one BIO_sock_info call.

ptr.note: The caller temporarily stores a borrowed BIO_ADDR pointer in the union; BIO_sock_info writes the pointed-to address but neither retains nor frees it. Zero-initialized and explicitly cleared unions show null is representable, though the ADDRESS operation requires non-null.

types.name: addrinfo
types._comment_agent: The layout has multiple allocation origins: system result chains use freeaddrinfo, while OpenSSL-created AF_UNIX nodes use BIO_ADDRINFO_free. The type therefore needs allocation-specific owner strategies rather than one unconditional CDropped implementation.

ptr.note: Optional variable-sized socket-address storage belongs to the result node and is released with the chain; OpenSSL-created AF_UNIX nodes instead pair the same layout with BIO_ADDRINFO_free.
Optional NUL-terminated canonical-name storage belongs to a getaddrinfo result node and is released with its result chain.
A result node links to the remaining owned result chain. The enclosing chain's matching releaser consumes all linked nodes; projected access must borrow the tail from the head.

types.name: asn1_object_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_OBJECT conditionally owns its names and encoded bytes according to ASN1_OBJECT_FLAG_DYNAMIC_STRINGS/DATA. Built-in objects borrow immutable static tables, while transient non-dynamic objects may borrow caller storage; all three pointers are nullable.

ptr.note: A length-byte immutable OID buffer. DYNAMIC_DATA selects owned storage; built-in objects borrow static table bytes. The source states data remains const after initialization.
Owned and freed when DYNAMIC_STRINGS is set; otherwise built-in objects borrow immutable process-lifetime names. Transient stack objects may also borrow caller strings only for the enclosing call.
Owned and freed when DYNAMIC_STRINGS is set; otherwise built-in objects borrow immutable process-lifetime names. Transient stack objects may also borrow caller strings only for the enclosing call.

types.name: asn1_string_table_st
types._comment_agent: This is a plain scalar table record. ASN1_STRING_TABLE_get returns library-owned borrowed storage, and individual records have no unconditional public destructor because the global dynamic table and the static standard table own them.

types.name: bignum_st
types._comment_agent: bignum_st.d is a mutable dmax-word buffer. Normal expanded BIGNUMs own it, while BN_FLG_STATIC_DATA covers static tables and borrowed word buffers such as BN_with_flags/bn_set_static_words.

ptr.note: Owned dynamic or secure dmax-word allocation unless BN_FLG_STATIC_DATA is set; static and view BIGNUMs borrow the buffer. Empty BIGNUMs may have null d.

types.name: bio_method_st
types._comment_agent: BIO_meth_new allocates the method and owns its duplicated NUL-terminated name; static method tables borrow static names and callbacks. Callback slots are nullable program-lifetime function pointers and do not own code storage.

ptr.note: Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Nullable program-lifetime function pointer.
Owned for BIO_meth_new results and borrowed-static in static method tables; BIO_meth_free is used only for dynamically allocated tables.

types.name: bio_msg_st
types._comment_agent: BIO_MSG is a non-owning scatter/gather descriptor. No lifecycle routine frees the descriptor or any pointer field.

ptr.note: Borrowed byte buffer bounded by data_len. sendmmsg reads it; recvmmsg writes received bytes into it. NULL is accepted for an empty/no-buffer message.
Optional caller-owned BIO_ADDR. Datagram receive paths fill or clear it; send paths may read it.
Optional caller-owned BIO_ADDR. It is read as a destination on send and filled as a source address on receive.

types.name: bio_poll_descriptor_st
types._comment_agent: The union is non-owning and governed by type. Custom discriminants do not specify whether the shared bits are interpreted as pointer or uintptr_t.

ptr.note: Type-discriminated application-defined cookie. The OpenSSL tree does not dereference this union arm, so pointee mutability is intentionally undetermined.
Borrowed SSL handle selected by BIO_POLL_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_SSL. SSL_poll treats NULL as a no-op and otherwise invokes mutating SSL/QUIC operations without taking ownership.

types.name: bio_st
types._comment_agent: BIO is refcounted through references. libctx and method are retained borrows; next_bio/prev_bio are non-owning chain links. cb_arg and callback_ex are application-provided borrows. ptr is method-specific and may be either owned or borrowed depending on the BIO_METHOD and shutdown policy.

ptr.note: Optional function pointer supplied by the application; BIO does not own executable storage.
Application callback cookie retained verbatim; despite char spelling it is not required to be a NUL-terminated string.
BIO_new_ex stores the library context without taking a reference; it must remain live while method operations use it.
BIO_new_ex retains the const method descriptor without cloning or freeing it; callers keep dynamic BIO_METHOD objects alive.
Doubly-linked BIO chain link; BIO_free does not release it and BIO_free_all traverses and releases each node separately.
Doubly-linked BIO chain link; it carries no independent reference count.
Type-erased method data: concrete BIO_METHOD create/destroy and the shutdown flag decide whether it is owned, borrowed, a singleton, or a buffer.

types.name: hostent
types._comment_agent: hostent has no independent lifecycle primitive. Its pointer fields borrow static resolver storage, caller-provided reentrant storage, or the surrounding fallback object's storage; callers must not free them.

ptr.note: Borrowed NULL-terminated array; each non-null element borrows h_length address bytes from the host database result. No observed consumer writes through it.
Borrowed NULL-terminated array of borrowed NUL-terminated aliases; no observed consumer writes through it.
Optional borrowed official host name. The fallback initializer stores NULL and no observed consumer writes through the string.

types.name: in6_addr
types._comment_agent: in6_addr is a by-value 16-byte address with no pointer fields and no lifecycle primitive.

types.name: lhash_st
types._comment_agent: The public OPENSSL_LHASH is opaque. Its private bucket array is allocated, resized, mutated, and freed by crypto/lhash/lhash.c; each non-null slot owns a separately allocated node, while node payload ownership remains with callers. Callback fields are borrowed executable-code pointers: comp/hash are made non-null by OPENSSL_LH_new defaults, and thunk callbacks may remain null.

ptr.note: Owned bucket array of num_alloc_nodes node pointers. OPENSSL_LH_flush frees every non-null node and OPENSSL_LH_free then frees the array; expand/contract reallocates and mutates it. Individual slots may be null. Node data payloads are not owned by the table.
Borrowed comparison callback; OPENSSL_LH_new substitutes strcmp when its argument is null.
Optional borrowed thunk callback installed by OPENSSL_LH_set_thunks.
Optional borrowed do-all-argument thunk installed by OPENSSL_LH_set_thunks.
Optional borrowed do-all thunk installed by OPENSSL_LH_set_thunks.
Borrowed hash callback; OPENSSL_LH_new substitutes OPENSSL_LH_strhash when its argument is null.
Optional borrowed thunk callback installed by OPENSSL_LH_set_thunks.

types.name: obj_name_st
types._comment_agent: OBJ_NAME records own only their header allocation inside o_names.c. Their public name/data fields borrow caller-managed immutable NUL strings; there is no public per-record destructor or clone operation.

ptr.note: OBJ_NAME_add stores caller-managed const data without copying it. Non-alias entries may carry NULL; optional type-specific free callbacks, not OBJ_NAME itself, govern any external storage.
OBJ_NAME_add stores the caller's const NUL-terminated name without copying it; registered callbacks receive that borrowed pointer.

types.name: ossl_init_settings_st
types._comment_agent: Both optional string fields are independently owned malloc-family strings. OPENSSL_INIT_free releases both and then the settings allocation.

ptr.note: OPENSSL_INIT_set_config_appname duplicates the input with strdup, replaces and frees the old allocation; OPENSSL_INIT_free frees it.
OPENSSL_INIT_set_config_filename duplicates the input with strdup, replaces and frees the old allocation; OPENSSL_INIT_free frees it.

types.name: stack_st
types._comment_agent: The public OPENSSL_STACK is opaque. Its private data field owns the resizable pointer array, while each type-erased element is either caller-borrowed or transferred for later OPENSSL_sk_pop_free according to the API path. Plain OPENSSL_sk_free never frees elements. Comparator and thunk fields are optional borrowed executable-code pointers with static lifetime.

ptr.note: Optional borrowed comparison thunk installed by OPENSSL_sk_set_cmp_thunks.
Optional borrowed comparator callback, installed at construction or by OPENSSL_sk_set_cmp_func and invoked only while stored.
Optional borrowed element-copy thunk installed by OPENSSL_sk_set_copy_thunks.

Owned allocation of num_alloc type-erased pointer slots, nullable until capacity is reserved. Stack operations resize it and replace/move slots. Elements are borrowed on ordinary stack paths, but callers may transfer them to an owning stack that is consumed with OPENSSL_sk_pop_free. The const element pointees are not mutated through this field.
Optional borrowed element-free thunk installed by OPENSSL_sk_set_thunks.
Consumes a dynamic object and its conditional fields; for a built-in static object the destructor is intentionally a no-op. NULL is accepted.
Required NUL-terminated configuration token; read only for this call.
BIO_ADDR_dup only reads the source during the call and accepts NULL.
A non-NULL result is a fresh deep copy owned by the caller; allocation or copy failure yields NULL.
BIO_ADDR_free consumes one BIO_ADDR allocation; NULL is accepted through OPENSSL_free.
BIO_ADDR_new returns a fresh initialized allocation owned by the caller, or NULL on allocation failure.
Optional borrowed output slot. On successful accept it receives a newly allocated OpenSSL-owned NUL string; failure may write NULL.
Required callback, invoked synchronously and never retained.
Input byte buffer of len bytes; NULL is only usable when len is zero and it is not retained.
Optional opaque callback context passed through synchronously and never retained.
Required callback, invoked synchronously and never retained.
Optional opaque callback context passed through synchronously and never retained.
Input byte buffer of len bytes; NULL is only usable when len is zero and it is not retained.
Consumes one BIO reference; null is explicitly accepted.
Required NUL-terminated host/service input; the legacy non-const signature does not mutate it.
Required writable output buffer of exactly four bytes for an IPv4 address.
Required NUL-terminated host name read for the call.
Required output slot written on successful lookup.
Optional service string; NULL is rejected without dereference.
Consumes a dynamic BIO_METHOD allocation; NULL is explicitly accepted.
Borrowed NUL-terminated input duplicated during the call.
Fresh mutable method allocation, or NULL on allocation failure; released by BIO_meth_free.
BIO_new retains the method descriptor, so it must outlive the returned BIO.
Returns one newly constructed BIO reference or null on failure.
Command-specific in/out scalar. In-tree callers pass a live int/unsigned-long slot for FIONBIO; type and request coupling is a caller obligation.
Transient live BIO borrow whose reference counter is incremented; zero reports failure.
Consumes a caller-owned BIGNUM, clearing its dynamic words and malloced header before release; NULL is accepted.
Reads a live source for this call; NULL is accepted and returns NULL.
Returns a fresh independently owned deep copy preserving secure allocation, or NULL on input/allocation failure.
Consumes a caller-owned BIGNUM allocation and its non-static word buffer; NULL is accepted.
Transient optional source-file string forwarded to CRYPTO_free.
Consumes a nullable OpenSSL allocation after cleansing the supplied byte length; applicable to scalar storage, buffers, and strings.
Transient optional source-file string used only by a configured free callback.
Consumes a nullable allocation obtained from the active OpenSSL allocator; used for scalars, counted buffers, and strings.
Transient source byte buffer of the supplied size; NULL is rejected.
Transient optional source-file string forwarded to the allocator.
Fresh byte-for-byte copy of siz bytes, owned by the caller and releasable with CRYPTO_free; NULL on invalid input or allocation failure.
Transient optional source-file string used on the ordinary-allocation fallback.
Consumes nullable secure or ordinary OpenSSL storage; secure storage is cleansed by actual size and ordinary storage by num bytes.
Transient optional source-file string used on the ordinary-allocation fallback.
Consumes nullable secure or ordinary OpenSSL storage; secure allocations are cleansed using their recorded actual size before release.
Transient optional source-file string forwarded to the OpenSSL allocator.
Transient NUL-terminated source string; NULL is accepted and yields NULL.
Fresh NUL-terminated copy allocated by the active OpenSSL allocator and releasable with CRYPTO_free; NULL on NULL input or allocation failure.
Transient optional source-file string forwarded to the OpenSSL allocator.
Transient source buffer readable for up to s bytes; no NUL is required within that bound, and NULL yields NULL.
Fresh NUL-terminated copy of at most s source bytes, allocated by OpenSSL and releasable with CRYPTO_free; NULL on NULL input or allocation failure.
Optional lookup name; NULL returns NULL without dereference.
Optional borrowed registry payload. Although declared char*, the payload is type-erased and may be an object pointer; it remains registry-owned and may be invalidated by removal/cleanup.
Required sorted array of num fixed-size records; read only.
Required comparator invoked synchronously and never retained.

Optional NUL-terminated input copied into the global object registry on success and never retained directly.
Optional NUL-terminated input copied into the global object registry on success and never retained directly.

Dynamic inputs produce a fresh deep copy; non-dynamic inputs return the same source pointer. Either non-null result may be passed to ASN1_OBJECT_free, but the same-pointer case remains borrowed from o.
Optional digest-NID output slot written on success.
Optional public-key-NID output slot written on success.
Required NUL-terminated object name read during lookup.
Optional library/registry-owned NUL string; dynamic entries can be invalidated by registry cleanup, so safe wrappers copy it.
Optional library/registry-owned NUL string; dynamic entries can be invalidated by registry cleanup, so safe wrappers copy it.
Required NUL-terminated object name read during lookup.
Consumes the settings allocation when non-NULL, freeing both owned strings and the header.
Returns a newly malloc-allocated, initialized settings object or NULL.
Optional input string is copied with strdup and remains caller-owned.
Mutably borrows settings for the call and replaces its owned appname.
Mutably borrows settings for the call and writes flags.
Optional input string is copied with strdup and remains caller-owned.
Mutably borrows settings for the call and replaces its owned filename.
Consumes and frees a complete OPENSSL_LHASH allocation after flushing owned nodes; null is accepted as a no-op.
Optional borrowed comparison callback; null selects strcmp. The callback code has static executable lifetime.
Optional borrowed hash callback; null selects OPENSSL_LH_strhash. The callback code has static executable lifetime.
Returns a newly allocated, initialized table on success; caller releases it with OPENSSL_LH_free.
Borrowed type-erased first element, valid only for the callback invocation.
Borrowed type-erased second element, valid only for the callback invocation.
Borrowed type-erased source element read during deep copy.
Returns a fresh independently owned element allocation, or NULL on copy failure.
Optional borrowed element-copy callback. NULL selects a shallow element-pointer copy; otherwise it is called only during this operation.
Borrowed cleanup callback for already-copied elements after a copy failure. It may be NULL only for the shallow-copy mode or when failure cleanup cannot call it.
Transient optional source stack; NULL produces a new empty stack.
Fresh stack owned by the caller; with a copy callback it owns independent copied elements, while NULL copy_func produces a shallow pointer copy.
Transient optional source stack. The routine reads it during the call; NULL produces a new empty stack.
Fresh stack and pointer-array allocation owned by the caller and releasable with OPENSSL_sk_free; element pointers are copied but remain unowned.
Consumes a complete nullable OPENSSL_STACK allocation and its pointer array; elements are deliberately not freed.
Consumes an optional type-erased element allocation exactly once when invoked by stack cleanup.
Optional borrowed comparator stored in the returned stack; callback code has static executable lifetime.
New initialized stack owned by the caller and releasable with OPENSSL_sk_free; NULL on allocation failure.
New initialized stack without a comparator, owned by the caller and releasable with OPENSSL_sk_free; NULL on allocation failure.
Optional borrowed comparator stored in the returned stack; callback code has static executable lifetime.
New initialized stack with requested initial capacity, owned by the caller and releasable with OPENSSL_sk_free; NULL on allocation failure.
Borrowed element destructor callback. It must be callable whenever a non-null element is present and is used only during this call.
Consumes a nullable stack, releases each non-null element through func or the stored thunk, then releases the stack.

For a heap context, OSSL_LIB_CTX_free deinitializes and releases the allocation. NULL and the process-global default context are accepted and retained, so the general C contract also has a static borrowed path; Rust owners only adopt constructor results.
OSSL_LIB_CTX_new allocates and initializes a fresh context; NULL reports allocation or initialization failure. The caller owns the returned context and releases it with OSSL_LIB_CTX_free.
Generic allocator release: accepts nullable scalar, buffer, or NUL-string allocations and consumes them.
Consumes a nullable OpenSSL byte buffer, cleansing size bytes when pedantic zeroization is configured and otherwise releasing directly.
Transient non-null NUL-terminated source string; passing NULL is outside strdup's contract.
Fresh malloc-family NUL-terminated copy owned by the caller and releasable with free; NULL on allocation failure.
